To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the SVM classifier combined to the 12 most discriminating PET and CT features achieves the best classification performance with a value of area under the receiver operator characteristic curve of 0,91.

the SVM classifier with the best combination of 12 PET and CT features achieves the best classification performance, that the SVM classifier trained with the PET features only achieves a performance close to the best performance, and that the SVM classifier based on the PET features only performs better than the SVM classifiers trained on the multimodality features.

a computer-aidation system based on support vector machine (with a feature set of 105 PET/CT characteristics) was able to discriminate between hyper-metabolic cancer lesions and noncancerous but hypermetabolic lesions in FDG PET exams of lymphoma with a high accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of computer-aided staging of lymphoma patients with PET/CT imaging based on textural information.
the development and evaluation of a computer-aidized diagnostic system for discriminating between hypermetabolic lesions of cancerous origin and noncancerous hypermetabolic lesions.

the development of a novel computer-aided staging system for lymphoma patients based on FDG PET/ CT imaging that can be used to assist the physician in discriminating between hypermetabolic lymphomatous lesions and nonlymphomatoseous lesions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a computer-aidized system combining PET and CT characteristics, including both clinical and more advanced texture features, can help in the diagnosis of lymphomas.

the SVM classifier with feature selection based on the combination of filter methods, using 12 PET and CT features, provides the best detection performance in discriminating lymphomatous lesions from nonlymphomatose lesions in FDG PET imaging.

the SVM classifier based on the combination of 12 PET and CT features is a promising tool for the discrimination between lymphomatous and suspicious nonlymphomatou regions of interest in FDG PET and CT imaging of lymphoma patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed computer-aided system can be used as a decision support tool for the discrimination between cancerous and non-cancerous lesions.
a computer aided diagnosis system for staging lymphoma patients based on PET/CT imaging and SVM classification is promising for the detection of hypermetabolic cancerous lesions.
we have developed a new system for the detection of lymphoma lesions based on FDG PET/ CT imaging that can be used to help the physician in staging patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a computer-aidized diagnosis system based on the combination of a SVM classifier with PET and CT features can help radiologists in discriminating lymphoma lesions from noncancerous hypermetabolic lesions.

the proposed SVM classifier combined with an original feature selection method and the use of multimodality PET and CT features allows the design of a computer-aidized diagnostic tool to assist physicians in discriminating between cancerous and noncancerous lesions in FDG PET and CT exams of lymphoma patient.

the combination of the most discriminant PET, CT and texture features allows to improve the classification performance of lymphomatous lesions compared to the classification performance based on PET and CT features only.
